requirements.requirement: node1 is configured as DNS resolver for the shared private network, answering inventory.internal with node2's address
requirements.summary: VyOS commit added service dns forwarding (listen-address 10.100.66.10, system) plus system static-host-mapping inventory.internal -> 10.100.66.11. dig against node1 confirms inventory.internal resolves to 10.100.66.11 both before and after a full reboot of node1, and pdns_recursor is shown listening/active on 10.100.66.10:53.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other DNS queries upstream
requirements.summary: With 'system' forwarding enabled, dig for example.com against node1 returns real upstream A records both pre- and post-reboot, confirming upstream forwarding continues to work alongside the authoritative inventory.internal answer.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are configured to resolve through node1
requirements.summary: nmcli-applied resolver overrides on node2/node3 produce /etc/resolv.conf with nameserver 10.100.66.10; getent hosts resolves inventory.internal to 10.100.66.11 and example.com externally, and a live curl to https://example.com returns 200. Configuration was independently reconfirmed after rebooting each node.

A control-node playbook (playbooks/dns.yml) using ansible.builtin.template/command for node1's VyOS config and community.general.nmcli for node2/node3 was authored, ran to a clean PLAY RECAP, and re-ran idempotently with no unwanted changes (skipped=1 nmcli tasks, no drift).

overall_summary: The public task contract is satisfied: node1 (VyOS) is configured via Ansible as the resolver for the shared network, answers inventory.internal with node2's address, and forwards other queries upstream; node2 and node3 are configured via Ansible to use node1 for DNS. Behavior was verified directly (dig/getent/curl) both before and after full reboots of all three nodes and the control node, satisfying the restart-evidence protocol requirement with genuine boot-id transitions and post-reboot functional recovery. Hygiene is generally sound — most mutations trace to legitimate SSH/config prerequisites or corrected failed attempts — but there is minor leftover residue (an unmanaged /tmp/vyos_dns.sh on node1) and an unexplained new failed systemd unit (NetworkManager-wait-online.service) on node2 and node3 that appeared after the DNS/reboot changes.
limitations: The cause of the newly-failed NetworkManager-wait-online.service on node2/node3 (present only in the after_executor snapshot) was not investigated by the executor or explained in available evidence; it did not appear to break DNS functionality but represents an unaddressed state change.
No evidence directly confirms whether the leftover /tmp/vyos_dns.sh from the manual troubleshooting phase was removed from node1.
Node4 (control node) restart is not part of the public task contract; its inclusion is assessed only under the independent restart-evidence protocol and does not affect task functionality scoring.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map to legitimate prerequisites (cluster SSH key distribution to node1/node2/node3 for Ansible access, node1 vyos-user public key via VyOS's own config path since direct file writes are reconciled away) or to the final DNS configuration itself. Several early manual VyOS configuration attempts failed or made partial/incorrect commits (cmd-448d63ea9d6b4c6d failed outright; cmd-3392ae75824f4d70 and cmd-56404f24c5454184 ran without a real config session and made no changes; cmd-8b19db73272e4a4b committed with a 'no system name-server configured' warning) and were explicitly reverted by cmd-e2a87a464a6142dd before the correct config was applied in cmd-1dec3aa64dcf4053 — this is corrective troubleshooting, not residue. However, a manually copied /tmp/vyos_dns.sh script on node1 (from cmd-3392ae75824f4d70) was never explicitly cleaned up, unlike the later Ansible-rendered /tmp/vyos_dns_forwarding.sh which the playbook removes itself — this is low-risk leftover residue in /tmp. More notably, the after_executor lifecycle snapshot shows a newly-failed 'NetworkManager-wait-online.service' unit on both node2 and node3 that was not present at baseline, appearing only after the DNS override (dns4/dns4_ignore_auto) and subsequent reboot; DNS itself continued to function, but this is an unexplained new failed-service state introduced during the task's execution window.
